sources: Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station, House Centipede fact sheet (K. Dugas): "They are fast runners that actively chase down prey. Like other centipedes, house centipedes have a pair of forcipules (modified pincer-like legs) located directly underneath their mouthparts which can either administer a venomous sting to prey or be used in self-defense." / "They are solely predators that actively hunt other arthropods such as cockroach nymphs, bed bugs, flies, ants, silverfish, spiders, and all other household pests." / "They have 15 pairs of long striped legs" / "In homes they are most likely to frequent basements, cellars, and first-floor bathrooms. They are nocturnal and incredibly wary." / "they will immediately flee if they are discovered"; https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/caes/documents/publications/fact_sheets/entomology/house_centipede_scutigera.pdf

Penn State Extension, House Centipedes (S. Jacobs, rev. M. Skvarla 2023): "House centipedes feed on silverfish, firebrats, carpet beetle larvae, cockroaches, spiders, and other small arthropods." / "During the daytime, the centipedes inhabit dark, damp locations in the home and come out at night to forage for prey." / "Adult house centipedes have 15 pairs of legs"; https://extension.psu.edu/house-centipedes

Penn State Extension, Longbodied cellar spider (Pholcus phalangioides): "This spider is commonly found in cellars, warehouses, garages, caves, and other dark, quiet, protected spots." / "The webs are an irregular mesh of threads." / "An unusual behavior is that the spiders will rapidly vibrate in a circular fashion in the web if threatened, making it difficult to see them."; https://extension.psu.edu/longbodied-cellar-spider

Utah State University Extension, Cellar Spiders: "common in basements, crawlspaces and behind HVAC units, furniture, pianos and other seldom-moved objects" / "make irregular cobwebs near windows, over pipes, or all over the ceiling and walls, especially in corners" / diet: "insects and other arachnids"; https://extension.usu.edu/planthealth/ipm/notes_nuisance/cellar-spiders
